title: Wave-based GPU provisioning plan by region (NA / EU / APAC) - 2026
body:
Summary:
This working sheet lays out a wave-based approach to provisioning additional GPU capacity across North America, Europe, and APAC for H1–H2 2026. The goal is to align supply with anticipated product demand (hosted API growth + Dedicated reservations + Private onboarding), keep regional utilization in the 65–80% target band, and preserve a 10–15% operational buffer for peak days and failover.

Context and guiding assumptions:
- Baseline demand estimate derived from usage model (hosted API 45% of tokens, Dedicated 35%, Private 20%) and recent month-over-month growth rates (hosted API +18%/mo, Dedicated +8%/mo, Private steady).
- Preferred GPU types per workload: H100 (latency-sensitive generation and large models), A100 (stable throughput), L4 (inference for small-embedding/low-cost routes).
- Target utilization: 70% target average across fleet; autoscaling should keep 55% min during off-peak and cap at ~90% during burst events.
- Lead times: cloud procurement + image validation + network setup ~ 6–8 weeks for standard regions, 10–12 weeks for APAC edge regions.
- Budget cap for committed capacity Q1–Q4 2026: internal planning cap (USD) — referenced in INFRA-482.

High-level rollout waves (proposed):
- Wave 0 (stabilize): 2025-12 — finalize sizing methodology, CI images, and test harness for new AZs.
- Wave 1 (core NA + EU): 2026-02 → bring online additional H100 and A100 pools targeted at Hosted API and Dedicated traffic.
- Wave 2 (APAC primary regions): 2026-04 → provision conservative H100 footprint + L4 pools for low-cost inference.
- Wave 3 (burst and capacity buffer): 2026-06 → reserve additional burst capacity and cross-region failover setups; enable preemptible pools for cost savings.

Per-region month-by-month snapshot (GPU cards, capacity units = 1 card):
- North America (NA):
  - Jan 2026 baseline: H100: 200, A100: 480, L4: 120 (avg util: 68%)
  - Feb 2026 (Wave 1 activation): +H100 80, +A100 120 -> H100:280, A100:600, L4:120 (proj util: 72%)
  - Mar–May: demand growth adjusts; autoscale rules added to keep avg util ~70%
  - Jun 2026 (Wave 3 buffer): +A100 60 (burst), enable preemptible pool +L4 40

- Europe (EU):
  - Jan 2026 baseline: H100: 120, A100: 320, L4: 80 (avg util: 66%)
  - Feb 2026 (Wave 1): +H100 40, +A100 80 -> H100:160, A100:400
  - Apr 2026: Add regional cache nodes + KV-prefetch to reduce peak token load on compute
  - Jun 2026: add +H100 20 as failover reserve

- APAC:
  - Jan 2026 baseline: H100: 40, A100: 120, L4: 60 (avg util: 74% — note higher burstiness in APAC evenings)
  - Apr 2026 (Wave 2): +H100 60, +L4 80 -> H100:100, A100:120, L4:140 (proj util: 68%)
  - Jun 2026: evaluate local dedicated bookings; if >3 enterprise signups, accelerate further H100 commitments

Quick capacity math (simplified):
- Token-hours per region projected growth → capacity requirement computed by benchmarking runs (see linked Confluence). We aim for headroom = 12% steady + 10% burst reserve = ~22% safety margin per region.

Operational controls and autoscaling rules (draft):
- Scale-up triggers: node-level CPU/GPU util >85% sustained 90s or request queue depth > 120s
- Scale-down: util <40% for 300s and no pending requests in queue
- Prefetch + KV cache warmup for top-50 routes before peak windows (NA: 09:00–18:00 PT, EU: 08:00–17:00 CET, APAC: 10:00–22:00 JST)
- Cost control: prefer preemptible for non-latency-critical routes, apply quantization profiles to lower-cost buckets where output quality acceptable

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: APAC lead times longer than estimated -> mitigation: early carrier/partner outreach and temporary traffic shift to EU with region-aware latency SLOs.
- Risk: Supply disruption for H100 SKUs -> mitigation: maintain cross-compatible A100 fallbacks, prepare quantized H100-lite variants, and pre-order via committed capacity where possible.
- Risk: Overprovisioning leading to wasted committed spend -> mitigation: staged rollouts with monthly capacity checkpoints and rollback policy to limit new commitments to 60% until 4-week utilization readouts confirm demand.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Q1: Approve preemptible vs committed split target per region (recommended: NA 25% preemptible, EU 30%, APAC 35%).
- Q2: Enterprise Dedicated lead times — how many pending contracts should trigger immediate front-loaded provisioning? (suggest trigger = 3 active LOIs).
- Q3: Acceptable percent of production traffic to route to cross-region fallback during APAC outages? (suggest default 20% with tiered failover).

Action items and owners (initial):
- Asha Patel: finalize procurement budget and commit sizes for Wave 1 (due 2026-01-15)
- Diego Alvarez: test new GPU images and autoscaler policy in staging (due 2026-01-30)
- Maya Chen: update routing policy and latency SLO docs; add region-aware monitoring dashboards (due 2026-02-10)
- Thomas Nguyen: run cost simulation for preemptible vs committed mixes and present tradeoffs (due 2026-01-25)
- Rina Saito: coordinate APAC datacenter partners and document lead times per availability zone (due 2026-02-28)

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- Numbers intentionally conservative for first-pass budgeting; expect adjustments after Wave 0 load tests.
- This sheet mixes rough counts with policy language — please point out if you want a separate pure spreadsheet export for finance.
- Refer to INFRA-482 and the provisioning playbook for the validation checklist and bootstrapping steps.

Changelog:
- 2025-11-20: initial draft (Asha)
- 2026-01-08: added per-region baselines and Wave 1 sizing (collab: Diego, Maya)
- 2026-02-12: updated APAC lead-time notes and action owners (Rina added)

Unresolved items to capture in follow-up sheet:
- Per-AZ capacity distribution (to be generated after provider quotes)
- Precise cost modeling per SKU vs. committed term length (60/36/12 months tiers)
- Integration checklist for Private deployments (networking/KMS)

End of sheet.
